note: RemoteSafe Stage 1 baseline risk library. Likelihood and consequence are 1-5 planning scales chosen by policy, not measured probabilities. Organisations may change ratings and thresholds; stop conditions and baseline mandatory controls cannot be switched off.

controls.label: Mechanical condition checked and pre-start inspection done
Tyres and spare tyre checked
Fuel filled and estimated range covers the longest leg
Recovery equipment carried (snatch strap, shovel, compressor)
First aid kit carried and in date
Fire extinguisher carried where required
Drinking water and emergency supplies for the whole party
Navigation and offline maps loaded
Mobile phone carried and charged
Satellite phone or satellite messenger carried
Device batteries charged, spare power carried
UHF radio fitted and working
Emergency contacts confirmed with the worker
Check-in times and method confirmed with the journey monitor
Communications tested before departure
Fatigue assessment done (sleep in last 24 and 48 hours)
Worker fit for work (no impairment, medication checked)
Licence and driving competency suit the vehicle and roads
Remote-area or 4WD training current
Weather, road and flood conditions reviewed on the day
Journey hazards and emergency instructions understood

hazards.title: Driver fatigue
hazards.description: Long or early driving can cause fatigue and microsleeps.

hazards.title: Excessive driving duration
hazards.description: Driving time in one day exceeds the organisation's limit.

hazards.title: Night driving
hazards.description: Part of the journey is planned in the dark, with reduced visibility and more wildlife.

hazards.title: Wildlife or livestock collision
hazards.description: Animals on the road, especially at dawn, dusk and night and on unfenced remote roads.

hazards.title: Unsealed roads
hazards.description: Loose surfaces, dust and reduced braking on gravel or dirt roads.

hazards.title: Corrugations and vehicle instability
hazards.description: Long unsealed sections with corrugations can cause loss of control and vehicle damage.

hazards.title: Flooded roads and causeways
hazards.description: Creek, river and causeway crossings can flood quickly. Never drive into floodwater.

hazards.title: Road closure or restriction on the route
hazards.description: A closure or load or access restriction recorded on a route leg.

hazards.title: Severe weather
hazards.description: Storms, cyclones, flooding rain or fire weather on the route.

hazards.title: Extreme heat
hazards.description: Heat stress and dehydration, worse after a breakdown in a remote area.

hazards.title: Vehicle breakdown
hazards.description: A breakdown far from help leaves the party stranded.

hazards.title: Inadequate communication coverage
hazards.description: Parts of the route may have no mobile coverage.

hazards.title: Remote or isolated work
hazards.description: Help is far away and response times are long.

hazards.title: Medical emergency
hazards.description: Injury or illness far from medical care.

hazards.title: Dangerous wildlife
hazards.description: In northern Australia, creek and river crossings and waterholes may be estuarine crocodile habitat.

hazards.title: Inadequate recovery equipment
hazards.description: Getting bogged or stuck on unsealed roads without the gear to recover.

hazards.title: Lack of emergency response capability
hazards.description: Very remote areas may have no nearby ambulance, police or fire service.

hazards.title: Delayed rescue
hazards.description: Long gaps between check-ins delay the alarm being raised.

hazards.title: Working alone
hazards.description: No one else in the vehicle to help or raise the alarm.

hazards.title: Insufficient food, water or fuel
hazards.description: A leg longer than the safe fuel range, or not enough water and food for a delay.
